thread:
alex: Quick thread — thinking about scheduling entropy vs deterministic assignment for continuous batching. Do we want randomness to avoid pathological alignment, or deterministic lanes to make observability and debugging simpler?

jia: Randomness buys avoidance of synchronized tails but makes reproducing slow requests harder. :thinking_face:

noah: Agree. We saw a case where two tenants always aligned and caused headroom storms. Randomizing admission resolved it but made root cause hard to trace.

sam: What if we do deterministic + controlled jitter? e.g., stable hash -> lane, but apply tiny time jitter on enqueue to break micro-alignment.

alex: That feels promising. Small jitter (<5ms) probably won't impact p50 but could smooth p99 spikes. Any ideas on proving it?

jia: We can simulate with our trace replay harness. Two configs: pure deterministic, deterministic+jitter, fully random. Compare: batch sizes, queue length variance, tail latency.

noah: Also need to consider KV cache locality. Deterministic lanes make it easier to warm KV cache affinities. Jitter might scatter cache hits.

sam: Right — tradeoff: tail smoothing vs cache hit rate -> token cost. Maybe bias jitter to keep affinity: only jitter within the tenant's assigned lane window (so it stays same lane).

alex: So lane assignment -> keeps KV cache affinity, jitter just alters enqueue time. Good. What about fairness signals during preemption?

jia: We had issues with split decisions when admission controller and eviction were slightly out of sync. Two nodes decided to preempt same tenant differently and caused thrash.

noah: That's the split-brain risk I worry about. We need a canonical eviction owner per queue (lease token) and an eventual consistency window where preemptions are applied only by the lease owner.

sam: Lease owner + soft-quiesce period before hard kills. E.g., owner signals preempt -> 50ms drain -> if not drained, owner initiates eviction. That reduces double-eviction races.

alex: Can we unify that with the existing heartbeat/lease system? Keep leases but add a short grace window config per lane.

ops-bot: Reminder: there's an existing metric `batcher.preempt.requests` that will need tagging for owner-id if we add this.

jia: Good call. Telemetry needs owner_id + decision_reason so postmortem shows why eviction happened (latency SLO vs headroom).

noah: Another angle: admission contracts should include a `deadline_hint` field. If callers provide it, scheduler can prioritize by effective deadline to reduce wasted work.

sam: Yes — prefer earliest-deadline-first within a lane, but keep a fairness cap so a single tenant doesn't monopolize. Implement: EDF + token bucket per-tenant.

alex: EDF + tenant token buckets + lane-level batching seems like a lot of knobs. We need a simple default that works 90% of time. Suggestions for sane defaults?

jia: Default: deterministic lane by hash, small enqueue jitter, EDF not enabled by default (but honor deadline_hint by demoting non-deadline), tenant token bucket = burstable but small steady rate, preempt grace = 50ms.

noah: For KV cache-sensitive workloads, provide a config toggle: `affinity_strict=true` which disables jitter and favors hot-path cache locality. Document cost tradeoffs.

sam: Also add an escape hatch: admin can pin critical tenants to dedicated micro-queues to guarantee tail behavior.

alex: Looks like action items: (1) run replay sim for three configs, (2) add owner_id tag to preempt metrics, (3) prototype lease-owner grace window, (4) add `deadline_hint` support in admission API.

jia: I'll take (1) and (4).

noah: I'll do (2) and sketch lease-owner changes for (3).

sam: I'll draft doc for `affinity_strict` and admin pinning UX.

alex: Thanks. If we keep messages short we can merge this into the RFC follow-up doc. One more question: how aggressive should the jitter distribution be — uniform or exponential tail?

jia: Uniform small jitter first. If we need more de-correlation, try a skewed distribution that penalizes requests arriving at exact boundary times. But start simple.

noah: Agreed. Start with uniform +/- 5ms and iterate based on sim results.

sam: I'll add the metric changes to the observability backlog so we can track before/after. :white_check_mark:

alex: Great thread. Keeping it small helped. Will sync next week with sim outputs.
